database.engine: Railway-hosted PostgreSQL (project db04e5b1, DATABASE_URL host caboose.proxy.rlwy.net)
database.note: Confirmed LIVE via `SHOW max_connections;` (=100) and `SHOW superuser_reserved_connections;` (=3) against production DB on 2026-10-18. The app's real ceiling is 97, NOT the Abacus platform 25/DB default — this app runs on its own Railway Postgres. The documented '88-vs-97 failure' is a pool bump that pushed worst-case total connections toward the 97 usable ceiling.

productionPools.notes: Dominant pool. Opens up to max on demand; idle conns closed after idleTimeoutMillis=30s. Under worker-isolation child-process mode the parent reserves PG_PARENT_RESERVE(=4) and each job child gets floor((PG_POOL_MAX-reserve)/WORKER_CONCURRENCY) — partitioned, never grown.

scriptPools_notInProd: server/scripts/*.ts and *.cjs create their own short-lived pools (max 2-5) for offline gates/benchmarks; they do NOT run inside the app/worker services and are excluded from the live budget.

appWideWorstCase.verdict: With default PG_POOL_MAX=20, even 2 app + 2 worker replicas (=106) EXCEEDS the 97 usable ceiling in the saturated worst case. This is exactly the 88-vs-97 class of failure.

candidates.dbConnections: 97 usable (BINDING). Saturating pools across replicas breaches this first.
candidates.workerConcurrency: Static 10 jobs/replica; each job fans ~100 sequential drizzle queries through the shared pool — bounded by pool max, not an independent ceiling.
candidates.llmApi: Governed separately by LLM_MAX_CONCURRENCY x replica_count against the provider account; not the DB-side constraint B6 addresses.

bindingBottleneck.conclusion: DB connections (97 usable) is the binding ceiling. B6 governs WORKER JOB CONCURRENCY against a connection budget so that effectiveConcurrency x replicaCount x connectionsPerJob + reservedOverhead can never exceed the budget as replicas scale.

derivedSafeBudget.rationale: Budget 90 sits safely under the 97 usable ceiling (matches server/db.ts guidance 'comfortably under ~90'). reservedOverhead=10 covers the app service's main pool share + worker control-plane (claim/heartbeat/reaper) + the small telemetry pools. connectionsPerJob=2 = PG_POOL_MAX(20) / static concurrency(10). HARD_MAX=10 pins the ceiling at today's static concurrency so dynamic mode can only ever LOWER concurrency as replicas grow, never raise it above the historical value.
derivedSafeBudget.note: B6 does NOT change any pool max in this WP (approval-gated tuned-matrix decision). It only derives safe per-replica worker concurrency from the known budget.
